why_not_city_wide: Rape is about 10 percent above the official PPD year-end table in both 2023 and 2024.
Robbery is about 17 to 20 percent above the official PPD year-end table in both 2023 and 2024.
Larceny is about 9 to 11 percent above the official PPD year-end table in both 2023 and 2024.
Motor vehicle theft is about 4 to 7 percent below the official PPD year-end table in both 2023 and 2024.
recommended_status.exact_next_action: Keep Philadelphia live for aggravated_assault and burglary only. Revisit murder only if a public criminal-homicide-only comparator is found.

source_contract.recommended_source_name: City of Philadelphia Crime Incidents / incidents_part1_part2
coverage_notes: The live Carto table spans from 2006-01-01 through at least 2026-03-24.
OpenDataPhilly publishes explicit yearly CSV resources for 2024, 2025, and 2026 and older year-specific CSV and SHP resources back to 2008 and earlier.
source_contract.official_description_summary: Crime incidents from the Philadelphia Police Department. Part I crimes include violent offenses such as aggravated assault, rape, arson, among others. Part II crimes include simple assault, prostitution, gambling, fraud, and other non-violent offenses.
official_terms_notes: The OpenDataPhilly page is published under City of Philadelphia terms of use and an as-is disclaimer.
The source is a live public data service rather than a frozen annual snapshot.

dc_key_non_uniqueness_examples: Some duplicated dc_key values are true duplicate homicide rows at the same location.
Some duplicated dc_key values span an earlier aggravated-assault row and a later homicide row, which makes dc_key unsafe as a strict incident dedupe key.
dedupe_contract.recommended_rule: Treat objectid as the stable public row key. Keep dc_key only as a case-linkage aid, not as the primary dedupe key.

spatial_contract.city_scope: All rows in the feed are already Philadelphia Police Department incidents, so no city-boundary screen is needed before city-level reconciliation.
recommended_assignment_rule: Use point_x and point_y or the_geom as the primary block-group assignment path.
Treat location_block as the fallback geocoding path for rows with null xy fields.
Because the feed is already citywide, missing-xy rows are a within-city spatial problem, not a city-membership problem.

mapping_risks: The feed exposes justifiable homicide separately, so murder requires a deliberate exclusion rule.
The public official table uses a different city publication surface and does not reconcile cleanly for all directly mapped categories.
The strongest exact mappings are burglary and aggravated assault.

ui_contract_notes: The public page loads an official citywide major-crimes table through the AJAX endpoint.
The public crime_statistics.js script sets the selectable minYear to 2023, so the current official year-end citywide table contract is strongest for 2023 forward.
official_reference_contract.official_disclaimer: All figures presented are based on preliminary Philadelphia Police Department crime data. This crime data is subject to reclassification upon further investigation.

published_reconciliation.reference_source_name: Philadelphia Police Department Crime Statistics citywide table
key_findings: Burglary is the strongest exact path: the feed differs from the official 2024 table by only -0.67 percent and from the 2023 table by only -0.16 percent.
Aggravated assault is also strong: the feed differs from the official 2024 table by +2.63 percent and from the 2023 table by +3.11 percent.
The official homicide comparator appears to include justifiable homicide. That makes murder nearly exact, but not yet an exact public comparator for the AGS/V2 murder object.
Rape, robbery, and larceny show stable material positive gaps, and motor vehicle theft shows a stable material negative gap.

city_wide: Stable multi-year reconciliation failures block city-wide use.
The official public table is strongest from 2023 forward, so older-year public reconciliation would need separate sourcing if the packet is expanded.
murder: The feed exposes criminal and justifiable homicide separately.
The official public comparator exposes only a single homicide line, which appears to include both.
motor_vehicle_theft: The feed is materially below the official citywide table in both 2023 and 2024.
No packet-local evidence yet explains the systematic undercount.

main_findings: Philadelphia does have a legitimate official city incident overlay candidate: the City of Philadelphia incidents_part1_part2 feed.
The feed has direct UCR-style offense fields, public coordinates, block-level address text, and citywide police coverage.
Objectid is a safe public row key; dc_key is not a safe primary dedupe key.
The Philadelphia Police public site exposes an official year-end citywide reconciliation endpoint through a public AJAX contract.
This packet supports offense-selective onboarding only, not city-wide onboarding.
The current exact/selective candidates are aggravated_assault and burglary.
